definition: An individual measurable input variable used by a model, such as the age or salary of a customer.
The correct output (target) of a training example in supervised learning.
A setting chosen before training, such as the learning rate or the number of trees, that is not learned from the data.
A value learned from the data during training, such as the weights of a linear regression.
A function that measures how far the predictions of the model are from the true values. Training tries to minimize it.
One complete pass through the entire training dataset.
A model that makes predictions by asking a sequence of yes/no questions about the features.
An ensemble of many decision trees trained on random subsets of the data, whose predictions are combined by voting or averaging.
An unsupervised algorithm that groups the data into k clusters by assigning each point to the nearest cluster center.
Rescaling feature values to a fixed range, usually 0 to 1.
Rescaling features so that they have mean 0 and standard deviation 1.
A regularization technique for neural networks that randomly turns off a fraction of the neurons during training.
